# HPublicShell

> A public landing-page frame: brand, a few links, an account action, and a quiet footer.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This reference describes repository source; package.json version: 0.2.0. Match it to the source/release you are using.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HPublicShell` from `@samishal1998/hearth-ui`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-public-shell>`.
- Individual constructor: `HearthPublicShellElement` from `@samishal1998/hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Layouts.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HPublicShell.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- Use for a landing page, guide, or public listing. It does not make underlying data public or grant access to linked applications.
- The default slot is page content. actions holds account/primary actions; navigation and footer can be replaced.
- Provide real URLs or handle navigate(id) with your application router.

## Public API

brand, logo, brandHref, active, footerText: string · items: NavItem[]

A `?` marks optional source props. A prop with a default may be omitted even when the source type is required. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    brand?: string;
    logo?: string;
    brandHref?: string;
    items?: NavItem[];
    active?: string;
    footerText?: string;
};
```

### Defaults

```ts
{
    brand: "hearth",
    brandHref: "/",
    items: () => [],
    footerText: "A little order for your digital world.",
  }
```

### Events

navigate(id)

```ts
type Emits = {
    navigate: [
        id: string
    ];
};
```

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose arguments as `event.detail`, an array. Listen directly on the element. Native DOM events such as `click` keep their normal payloads.

### Slots

brand, navigation, actions, default, footer

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Custom elements do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base, header, content, footer

Use `hearth-public-shell::part(part-name)` for an exposed part, or inherited `--h-*` tokens for system-level styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Supporting types

```ts
export interface NavItem {
    id: string;
    label: string;
    icon?: string;
    href?: string;
    badge?: string | number;
    disabled?: boolean;
}
```

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { HPublicShell, HButton, HPageHeader } from '@samishal1998/hearth-ui';
import '@samishal1998/hearth-ui/styles.css';
const items = [{ id: 'guide', label: 'Guide', href: '/guide' }];
</script>

<template>
  <HPublicShell brand="homestead" :items="items">
    <template #actions><HButton href="/login">Sign in</HButton></template>
    <HPageHeader title="A home for what we host." />
  </HPublicShell>
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point (use a `form` instead of `div` when demonstrating field submission):

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

The following is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a stylesheet link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Set array/object properties before connection when they should become reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@samishal1998/hearth-ui/elements';
import '@samishal1998/hearth-ui/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-public-shell');
Object.assign(element, {
  "brand": "homestead",
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "guide",
      "label": "Guide",
      "href": "/guide"
    }
  ]
});
element.innerHTML = "<hearth-button slot=\"actions\" href=\"/login\">Sign in</hearth-button>\n<hearth-page-header title=\"A home for what we host.\"></hearth-page-header>"; // Static example markup only; never inject untrusted HTML.
mount.append(element);
```
